tier_reason: First-party wall-clock A/B of the forked rav1e CLI against stock rav1e 564ae3b0, documented in rusty_av1e/docs/entropy-bricks.md (one synthetic testsrc2 clip, 7 interleaved rounds). The in-binary '--racecar stock' path and tests/profile_encode.rs are public, but the A/B script (scratchpad/ab.sh) is not in the repo, rustc version and flags are given only as 'identical flags', and the machine is never named, so it cannot be A.

corrections.workload: Real rav1e CLI: fork at opt-entropy HEAD 885a2887 vs stock rav1e 564ae3b0 (merge-base with xiph/master), both built with 'identical flags'; one synthetic 640x480, 60-frame ffmpeg testsrc2 clip, --speed 6 --quantizer 100 --tiles 1 --threads 1, 7 interleaved rounds, median wall-clock. A QP sweep (QP 60/100/160, 9/5/5 rounds) and the --racecar on ('nitro') runs (5 interleaved rounds) used the same clip on the same unnamed machine, which the ledger says has about 5% thermal noise.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Default --racecar off (byte-identical to stock rav1e, 262,180 B): median 7.588 s vs 6.911 s = 1.098x (per-round 1.072-1.117x); QP sweep 1.126x at QP 60, 1.099x at QP 100, 1.058x at QP 160. Opt-in --racecar on (rav1e's existing tx_domain_rate + tx_domain_distortion options plus the kernels): 4.586 s vs 7.745 s for the stock code path = 1.69x (1.61x over the byte-identical mode at 7.399 s), but the bitstream grows from 262,180 to 419,010 B (+60%) and PSNR drops from 44.50 to 42.22 dB (-2.28 dB) at the default tune; with --tune Psnr the probe measured +48% size and -1.13 dB. Decoder: no speed claim ('same as rav1d, profiled at its performance floor').
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated; the ledger says only that both binaries were 'built with identical flags'. rusty_av1e/Cargo.toml release profile uses lto = "thin" and debug = true; asm feature needs nasm; minimum rust-version 1.83.0, actual rustc version not given.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 0 stars, 1 fork, 112 commits; crates.io rusty_av1e 0.8.0 (1,270 downloads) and rusty_av1d 1.2.0 (1,492 downloads); README banner claims 1,002 active installs (not verifiable).
corrections.caveats: First-party, one synthetic 640x480 60-frame testsrc2 clip at speed 6, single thread and single tile; the machine, rustc version and flags are not named, and the A/B script (scratchpad/ab.sh) is not in the repo, although the binary keeps a '--racecar stock' mode that reproduces the stock code paths. The 1.10x gain is content dependent (1.058x to 1.126x by QP) and sits near the box's stated 5% thermal noise. The 1.69x mode is a quality trade, not a free speedup: it turns on rav1e's own tx-domain rate estimation (which stock rav1e leaves off at every speed) and costs +60% bitstream and -2.28 dB PSNR at the default tune; its 1.69x divides by a stock time taken from a separate sweep session. The numbers belong to this fork's own encoder kernels (B7a nz-map stencil, its AVX2 twin, Q2 branchless quantize), not to the vendored rav1e or rav1d projects; the decoder half (rav1d fork) has no speed claim. Not a GitHub fork; is_fork_of rav1e for the encoder, the decoder forks memorysafety/rav1d. Rust code with a Rust baseline (rav1e is not a wave-10 list baseline and not in the catalog). Part of Mata Network's 'Remade With Rust' initiative; README opens with an install-count banner and an advert. AV1 patent grant comes from the AOM Patent License 1.0 in rusty_av1e/PATENTS, separate from the BSD-2-Clause source license.

notes: Numbers are the fork's own encoder work measured against stock rav1e, so this is not a wrapper or duplicate of a listed project (rav1e and rav1d are not in the catalog); the decoder side carries no claim. Language is Rust (already set), a mismatch with the C++ language filter of the search. racecar.rs doc comment still describes the pre-remap default (racecar on), while README and ledger say the default is now off (byte-identical kernels).

tier_reason: README table (436x vs 291x, 213x vs 133x, 139x vs 145x realtime) comes from the public harness tools/bench_encode_3way.ps1 on a named CPU (i7-14650HX, Windows), but the rustc version and build flags are not stated and the libopus arm is whatever ffmpeg build is on PATH (-c:a libopus) with no version or flags, so first-party C rather than A.

corrections.workload: Process-level encode timing from tools/bench_encode_3way.ps1: rusty-opus via its examples/encode_ogg binary, libopus via 'ffmpeg -c:a libopus', FFmpeg's native encoder via 'ffmpeg -strict -2 -c:a opus'. Sources are corpus clips looped to 300 s and 150 s (speech_clean.wav at 48 kHz/32 kb/s audio, mus_guitar_st.wav stereo at 48 kHz/128 kb/s audio, fixtures/answer_16k.wav at 16 kHz/16 kb/s voip); the metric is the median slope t(300 s) - t(150 s) of Windows process CPU time, pinned to one core at High priority, 31 ABBA-alternated reps with a null arm; coding path (CELT or SILK) verified from TOC bytes.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated. Cargo release build of examples/encode_ogg with no [profile.release] override in Cargo.toml (edition 2024, rust-version 1.85, actual rustc not given); AVX2/FMA kernels selected at runtime. The libopus arm uses the ffmpeg build on PATH; its libopus version and build flags are not stated.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 5 stars, 4 forks, 148 commits; crates.io rusty-opus 0.9.1, 34,214 downloads (crate created 2026-07-29); README banner claims 4,827 active installs (not verifiable). Opus backend of Remade-With-Rust/remade_ffmpeg_rs.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers on one laptop CPU (i7-14650HX, Windows); rustc version, build flags and the libopus version/build are not stated. Settings are not matched: rusty-opus's encoder defaults to complexity 9 (src/lib.rs; encode_ogg does not change it) while FFmpeg's libopus wrapper defaults to compression_level 10 (libavcodec/libopusenc.c), so libopus runs at a higher complexity setting in the comparison; the effect on the ratio is not measured. The libopus and FFmpeg-native timings also include ffmpeg's per-sample WAV demux and Ogg mux work, which the slope does not cancel (probably small, not measured). Only three configurations are timed, two CELT and one SILK, each on one looped clip; the README tagline '~1.5x ... measured across 18 content classes' mixes the 18-class quality corpus with the 3-configuration speed test, and on the SILK path libopus is 4% faster. The quality claim uses PEAQ ODG on short public-domain and synthetic clips, as the README itself says. Performance fork of restsend/opus-rs (not a GitHub fork) whose own AVX2 SILK/CELT kernels and harness produce numbers distinct from opus-rs's, so it does not just inherit the upstream claims. Rust, not C++. Part of Mata Network's 'Remade With Rust' initiative; README opens with an install-count banner and an advert. Script header comment still describes 60 s/30 s clips, but its defaults (300 s/150 s) match the README.

notes: Not a copy of the opus-rs claims: opus-rs reported 2-28% wins on mono speech with a C-comparison bench missing from its repo, while rusty-opus has its own public 3-way harness and 1.50x/1.60x CELT figures, so it can stay a separate entry with is_fork_of restsend/opus-rs (orchestrator may still fold the two if one Opus-in-Rust row is preferred). Language is Rust (already set), a mismatch with the C++ language filter of the search. Opus/libopus is a wave-10 list baseline, so baseline_in_list true stands.

tier_reason: First-party terminal output pasted into the README (LAME 3.100 vs shineenc on an M1 Pro); no benchmark code beyond the CLI, compiler and flags not stated, and shineenc's own timer has one-second resolution, so C. Tier unchanged; verdict is downgrade because the derived 3.6x ratio is not supported by that timer.

corrections.claimed_speedup: M1 Pro MacBook Pro (2022-12-30), 5:18 stereo 44.1 kHz clip at 128 kb/s: LAME 3.100 'lame -b 128' 88.7x realtime (play/CPU; 3.55 s user, 3.609 s total) vs shineenc 'Finished in 00:00:01 (318.0x realtime)'. shineenc (src/bin/main.c) divides the clip duration by whole seconds from time(), so 318.0x only says the encode took less than 2 s of wall-clock: the page supports Shine being at least about 1.8x faster than LAME (at least 159x realtime vs 88.7x), not a precise 3.6x (derived from page data). Raspberry Pi (marked outdated): LAME 3.99.5 1.82x realtime (3:06 CPU) vs Shine 3.6x (1:35 wall), about 1.96x (derived from page data). Nexus 5: Shine 24.2x realtime (14 s), no LAME figure.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README runs; the default autotools build (Makefile.am) compiles with @CFLAGS@ -funroll-loops -fno-exceptions -Wall -O2 -fsigned-char.
corrections.hardware: Apple M1 Pro MacBook Pro (arm64); older runs on an unspecified Raspberry Pi model (LAME 3.99.5 32-bit) and a Google Nexus 5 (Shine only)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 422 stars, 77 forks, 294 commits (GitHub serves savonet/shine as toots/shine); ships JavaScript/WebAssembly and Android bindings; encoder CLI is the 'Liquidsoap version'; FFmpeg can link it as libshine (FFmpeg docs, search snippet only).
corrections.caveats: Quality trade-off: the README's Limitations section says the algorithm 'does not have any Psychoacoustic Model' and 'may not be exempt of bugs', and FFmpeg's libshine documentation (search snippet only) says Shine is not on par with LAME quality-wise; the page gives no quality numbers, while LAME ran its full psychoacoustic model at default qval=3, so the two encoders do different amounts of work. Shine's speed comes from fixed-point arithmetic and a simpler algorithm, which matters most on FPU-less targets. Timing: shineenc measures wall-clock with time() at one-second resolution (00:00:01 on the M1 Pro), whereas LAME's 88.7x is play/CPU time, so the M1 Pro ratio is only a lower bound of about 1.8x; the two runs also used different file names (/tmp/decoded.wav vs /tmp/bla.wav) of the same 5:18 length. First-party README timings, single runs, compiler and flags not given. License: COPYING is the GNU Library GPL v2 text and the source files carry no license headers or version statement, so LGPL-2.0-only vs -or-later cannot be settled from the repo; LGPL is OSI-approved (copyleft for modified library code). Last commits are from 2023-01-01. Same repository as toots/shine (savonet/shine redirects there).

notes: github.com/savonet/shine redirects to toots/shine (same 422 stars, 294 commits), so this record and the toots/shine record in batch 28 are one project; keep one and mark the other duplicate (toots/shine is the canonical GitHub URL, savonet/shine is the README's own link). The M1 Pro 318.0x figure is an artifact of a one-second timer, so the 3.6x headline should not be used as a precise ratio. License left as recorded because the only/or-later choice cannot be verified.
